findings.summary: "2,295 violations" is a 200-SEED figure recorded inside a 1,000-seed paragraph, with no seed count stated. RE-MEASURED on this tree: 2,295 at N=200, 11,110 at N=1,000. Same unstated scope in the M5.50 row at backlog.md:65, whose sentence opens "MEASURED at 1,000 seeds".
findings.detail: REPRODUCED out of tree (copy of sequencer/src/test/java compiled against the sequencer test runtime classpath; no file added to or changed in the repository). Baseline, 1,000 seeds, SWEEP_FAULTS, ROUNDS=120, PODS=3: every other figure in this block reproduces EXACTLY -- 85,458 readers (85.458/seed), 160,478 ack events (160.478/seed), 149.368 CONFIRMED/seed against 11.110 ACK/seed (93.08% CONFIRMED), mean clearances 8.5458x and 32.0956x, prefix minima 8.2000x at N=1 and 30.6000x at N=1, interior (N>=2) minima 8.3500x and 31.1000x so no interior prefix dips below the first, ACK-half mean 2.2220x and prefix minimum 1.1750x at N=8, and exactly 12 zero-ACK seeds (197, 222, 266, 573, 699, 718, 777, 803, 804, 870, 876, 974 -- the same 12 the file's own profile table calls zero-COMMIT, because ackOnly == commits on every one of the 1,000 seeds). The one figure that does not carry its scope is the violation count. Injecting M4.50's ack+1 defect at all three `acks.add(...acked(...))` sites and running `checkAckOrder` per seed: 2,295 violations over seeds 0-199, 11,110 over seeds 0-999 (one per ack, 988 seeds affected). The stripped-trace clearance is effectively scale-free (29.8290x at N=200, 29.8736x at N=1,000), so 29.83x survives the ambiguity; 2,295 does not -- it is 4.84x off at the file's own default SEEDS. The sentence sits fourteen lines below "160,478 ack events over 1,000 seeds", so 1,000 is the scope a reader carries into it. This is the same class of defect M5.30 exists to remove -- a number a later reader cannot reproduce from the stated conditions -- though a weaker instance, because it is not FALSE at its true scope and it gates no threshold. It touches no assertion. Recorded rather than fixed, per review.md rule 11.
findings.failure_scenario: The next person opening M5.50 re-runs the demonstration at the file's default 1,000 seeds, gets 11,110 violations against a recorded 2,295, and concludes the recorded measurement is stale or was taken on a different tree -- so they either re-derive the whole 93/7 argument from scratch or distrust the 149.37/11.11 split that is in fact exact. MEASURED: 2,295 at N=200, 11,110 at N=1,000, both with the three `acked(...)` sites emitting `sequence() + 1`.

findings.summary: M5.50's stated reason for "it cannot be isPositive() either" is the 12 zero-ack seeds, and MEASURED that evidence does not support it: the earliest zero-ACK seed is 197, so a cumulative `isPositive()` over the ACK half holds at EVERY prefix. The right reason -- workload-proportionality -- is already in this file eight lines above the floor.
findings.detail: The row reads: "THE ANSWER IS A SECOND FLOOR over `acks().stream().filter(AckEvent::isAck)`, respecting that 1.18x prefix minimum and those 12 zero-ack seeds -- which means it cannot be `isPositive()` either, for the reason M5.28 records about `gracefulReleaseRefusalsSeen`." M5.28's reason is that 38 events over 1,000 seeds is ~0.04 per seed, so a bare positive floor REDS at `-Dsweep.seeds=1` with no defect present. That reasoning does not transfer: MEASURED over 1,000 seeds, the ACK half is 11.11 per seed, seed 0 emits 8, and the twelve zero-ACK seeds are 197, 222, 266, 573, 699, 718, 777, 803, 804, 870, 876 and 974 -- none of them in a leading position. The sweep's only shortening knob is `-Dsweep.seeds=N`, which takes the prefix from seed 0 (`for (long seed = 0; seed < SEEDS; seed++)`), so there is no N for which the cumulative ACK count is 0. I checked all 1,000 prefixes: zero fail a positive floor. The conclusion (do not use `isPositive()`) is still right, for the reason CommitProtocolSweepTest.java:260-265 already gives -- `isPositive()` does not hold the WORKLOAD, since cutting ROUNDS from 120 to 3 leaves a sweep at 1/40th the work satisfying it -- and for the reason M5.28's own cell gives for this very floor ("`ackEvents`, the precedent, is `SEEDS * 5` and has no such problem"). Since the sentence also uses the twelve zero-ack seeds as a CONSTRAINT the new floor must respect, and they constrain nothing at the cumulative shape every floor in that method uses, an implementer checking the rationale finds it does not hold. Also worth pinning before that row is implemented: the row's headline "12 seeds emit ZERO ack events" means zero ACK-KIND events, while "160,478 ack events" fourteen lines earlier means the whole trace, and the minimum per-seed TOTAL is 45 (seed 489) -- no seed emits an empty trace. It is a todo row, nothing is asserted, so this is minor.
findings.failure_scenario: The implementer of M5.50 checks the stated rationale, measures that a cumulative `isPositive()` over the ACK half holds at every prefix from seed 0 (earliest zero-ACK seed is 197, and seed 0 emits 8), concludes the row's objection was wrong, and ships `assertThat(ackOnlyEvents).isPositive()`. That floor kills the strip mutation but loses the workload property every other floor in the method has: MEASURED precedent at CommitProtocolSweepTest.java:260-265 -- ROUNDS cut from 120 to 3 leaves a sweep at 1/40th the work green under positive-only floors. The ACK half then has no floor that separates a real run from a shallow one.
